ConstructiveDiagrams`CheckAmplitudes.Messages: {HoldPattern[CheckAmplitudes::args] :> "Expected diagram amplitudes, the ordinary channel rows returned by FactorizationAmplitudeChannels, a model, and valid comparison options.", HoldPattern[CheckAmplitudes::input] :> "`1`", HoldPattern[CheckAmplitudes::usage] :> "CheckAmplitudes[amplitudes, channels, model] checks physical residues against the ordinary rows returned by FactorizationAmplitudeChannels, automatically discovers apparent denominator poles, and tests high-energy growth and explicit Xi reference-spinor independence of the complete summed amplitude. Only supplied channels certify physical poles; other supported denominator poles are tested for cancellation while physical propagators remain nonzero. The physical comparison applies the sewing factor -1 from (i A_L)(i A_R)(i/PropDen)/i. HighEnergyCheck -> Automatic checks growth at sampled real, fixed-angle, momentum-conserving kinematics with external masses and couplings held fixed. Large supported reference-free expressions may certify a conservative all-spin upper bound, including massless bracket denominators whose leading coefficients are exactly nonzero in the sampled directions; ObservedPower remains missing when only ObservedPowerUpperBound is certified. Unsupported or inconclusive bounds use the exact Laurent expansion. HighEnergyBound -> Automatic assumes the renormalizable-tree bound E^(4-n); a numerical exponent overrides it, and HighEnergyCheck -> False disables this diagnostic. HighEnergySamples and HighEnergyTimeConstraint control the energy test. ReferenceCheck -> Automatic varies all literal Xi labels simultaneously at sampled conserved external kinematics away from physical poles, holding momenta and external spin states fixed. ReferenceSamples and ReferenceTimeConstraint control this test; ReferenceCheck -> False disables it. An expression without explicit reference spinors has no explicit Xi dependence; this is not a Ward-identity proof. ParameterRules -> Automatic uses numerical variables and dependent functions from the supplied model. An explicit rule list overrides selected model parameters; dependent functions are recomputed. Numerical values are used only for checking, leaving the amplitude symbolic. PASS denotes agreement, finiteness, acceptable growth or reference independence at the recorded kinematic samples, not a generic analytic proof. Opp Sign diagnoses an overall opposite sign in physical residues or a supplied Feynman comparison. Unsupported calculations and timeouts remain UNRESOLVED. Output -> \"HighEnergy\" shows energy samples, \"References\" shows reference comparisons, \"Residues\" shows physical and spurious-pole samples, \"Summary\" returns combined counts and \"Details\" retains all diagnostics. SpuriousPoles -> Automatic discovers denominators; a list overrides discovery and {} disables spurious checks. Set SpuriousPoles -> {}, HighEnergyCheck -> False and ReferenceCheck -> False for the legacy physical-only report. Samples, RandomSeed, ParameterRules and TimeConstraint control pole comparisons. Inputs remain unchanged and no amplitude correction or new interaction is added. FeynmanAmplitudes -> None optionally supplies an independent full Feynman amplitude, a mass-rule/expression pair, or a list of pairs. The full sums are compared at common conserved external on-shell momenta away from all internal propagator poles, with no internal-shell substitutions and no sewing sign or normalization fitted to the benchmark. Explicit Xi references vary independently between the two full sums. FeynmanSamples -> Automatic uses Samples and FeynmanTimeConstraint -> Automatic uses TimeConstraint. Output -> \"Feynman\" shows visible amplitude samples; Details includes FeynmanCheck. PASS and Opp Sign are sampled comparisons of all implicit massive-spin components, not generic analytic proofs. Raw supported Feynman tensors are converted automatically; use PrepareAmplitudes with FermionHelicities first when massless Dirac helicities must be supplied. Parallelization -> Automatic runs sufficiently large independent channel, spurious-pole and whole-amplitude checks on package workers. True requests parallel execution and False keeps the serial calculation. MaxKernels -> Automatic uses the available worker limit; a positive integer reduces it. The exact sample seeds and report ordering are preserved. Custom KinematicMap functions remain on the calling kernel without distributing user definitions. Failed worker calculations remain UNRESOLVED. Only Details includes execution metadata; ordinary tables are unchanged. RandomSeed -> Automatic chooses a time-based seed once per run without changing the caller's random stream. Details records the resolved RandomSeed; an explicit integer replays that run's sample choices. Supply FeynmanModel -> benchmarkModel when the benchmark comes from a separate model. Its numerical parameters are resolved only from that model; Automatic uses the third argument's model. Missing benchmark definitions remain UNRESOLVED rather than borrowing candidate values. ParameterRules may use string names such as \"Me\" -> 1 for local overrides."}

ConstructiveDiagrams`CompleteFactorizati.Messages: {HoldPattern[CompleteFactorization::args] :> "Expected amplitude pairs or an expression, ordinary factorization channels, a model and valid bounded-completion options.", HoldPattern[CompleteFactorization::usage] :> "CompleteFactorization[amplitudes, channels, model] constructs a bounded linear correction from the supplied diagram expressions and sewn channel expressions, solving all physical residues simultaneously. It accepts ordinary amplitude pairs, a prepared-expression report, or an expression. CorrectionBasis supplies correction directions; Automatic uses the input and channel expressions, not a universal amplitude ansatz. ChannelReferences -> Automatic constructs bounded alternative reference continuations, checking each on its selected cut. Without declared exchange symmetry, automatic completion first tries externally reduced whole physical-reference channels and grouped pole-bearing input terms, then falls back to literal input and channel terms within the same term and time limits. Explicit pole-free input terms are retained, not added as cancellation directions in the first attempt. ChannelReferences -> None keeps only the literal correction space. Recorded preparation references are tried when available. Failed independent validation samples supply further exact equations, up to MaxRefinements -> 3, with fresh subsequent validation. Only proven algebraically zero or exactly linearly dependent directions are removed without reducing the correction span; other residue-preserving directions remain available to CompleteHighEnergy. These sampled checks are not a generic analytic reconstruction or uniqueness proof. ReturnDetails -> False is the default: successful completion returns only the updated amplitude. ReturnDetails -> True retains the candidate, correction, affine family, CorrectionSpace, ChannelContinuations, RefinementHistory and validation, and takes precedence over Output. Output -> \"Details\" remains available for existing code. Unresolved completion normally returns a concise Failure[\"IncompleteAmplitude\", ...], without an unchecked candidate or embedded report. ParameterRules -> Automatic uses the supplied model's variables and dependent functions; an explicit rule list overrides selected parameters. Numerical substitutions affect the checks and fitting only, not the returned symbolic amplitude. No new interactions are inferred. RandomSeed -> Automatic chooses a time-based seed once for the complete stage, including its retries. Details records the resolved RandomSeed; an explicit integer retains reproducible sample choices. The default Output -> Amplitude returns {externalMassRules, expression}, containing only Mass[externalLeg] replacements and no internal-shell assumptions. Pass this pair directly to PrepareAmplitudes, CompleteHighEnergy or CheckAmplitudes. Output -> Expression requests the bare expression; detailed reports keep their separate Amplitude and ExternalMassRules fields. AlternativeChannels -> {} optionally supplies original or alternative compact channel rows. Only after automatic completion fails are their selected residues checked against the supplied channels and their correction directions tried within the remaining term and time budgets. The supplied channels remain the targets for fitting and independent validation; alternatives never replace them. AlternativeChannelFallback in the details records the checks and result. InputReweighting -> Automatic first tries a single fitted coefficient on the pole-bearing input, then on a candidate that retains one copy of exact signed terms shared across separate diagram records. Explicit additive terms without PropDen denominators retain their original multiplicity. These are proposed corrections, not identities for summing diagrams; every original physical-channel obligation must pass fresh coherent-spin and parameter validation. The attempts share at most one fifth of the remaining stage time, capped at 30 seconds. InputReweighting -> None disables them; explicit CorrectionBasis and ChannelReferences -> None retain their existing behavior. InputFitAttempts in details records coefficients, overlap counts and validation. No normalization is fitted by CheckAmplitudes or its Feynman comparison. ChannelCompanions -> Automatic tries a small source-derived space before the larger channel spaces. Eligible two-leg cuts contain one declared massless leg and an equal-mass anchor/exchange. After selected-cut source normalization, group by chain momentum-insertion count and peel the emitted leg from typed lower-amplitude composites while protecting the selected propagator. Peeling is a proposed correction, not an identity; only a full independently validated all-channel fit is accepted. Explicit regular input is retained, pure pole-free new directions are rejected, and all propagators must belong to the original physical target catalog. The attempts share one third of the remaining stage time, capped at 60 seconds, with at most 15 seconds for construction. ChannelCompanions -> None disables this attempt. RepresentativeSelection -> Automatic uses exact bounded coefficient cancellations to choose a simpler point in a validated free family, preserving all directions and all explicit regular coefficients. None retains the original particular point. Final cleanup accepts only whole-expression improvements. These cosmetic choices share the existing two-second post-validation budget. Details expose ChannelCompanions, ChannelCompanionFit and RepresentativeSelection with coordinate offsets. Pass detailed PrepareAmplitudes reports for either input, including the channel argument, to retain preparation provenance. Original channel rows remain the residue targets; simplified rows and their fixed-reference remainders supply corrections. PreparationRemainders -> Automatic tries bounded grouped preparation corrections after inexpensive input reweighting and before larger channel spaces. Ordinary pair virtuality identities expose factors without putting any assembled propagator on shell. Exact compatibility probes can reject a space early but never certify success; all original channels and held-out spin/parameter tests remain required. The attempt shares at most one fifth of the remaining stage clock, capped at 12 seconds, with at most four seconds for construction. Unsuccessful spaces leave the existing fallbacks intact. Retained common-reference sums may be tried as a final bounded continuation fallback; reference changes are not assumed to be off-cut identities. PreparationRemainders -> None disables these attempts. Explicit CorrectionBasis and ChannelReferences -> None retain their literal behavior. Details expose PreparationRemainders, PreparationRemainderFit, PreparationReferenceAttempts and ChannelPreparation. Ordinary preparation pairs and channel rows do not contain hidden history or a cache. PolePreference has the same choices as PrepareAmplitudes and ConstructAmplitude. Automatic inherits the requested choice from detailed preparation reports; an explicit choice overrides it. AllPhysical first tries a bounded space whose kinematic denominators are only supplied physical propagators. AllSpurious favors other-massless-leg reference continuations; Cyclic and ReverseCyclic retain their orientations; Mixed admits both physical and spurious choices; Xi and IndependentXi favor their corresponding external-reference prescription. None disables the preferred-space attempt. This is a representation preference, not a guarantee or a weaker check: every original target, zero-residue obligation, coherent spin component and independent validation remains required. All fitted correction freedom is retained for CompleteHighEnergy. No independent regular interaction is added, and explicit regular input stays fixed. The attempt reserves at most half the remaining stage clock, capped at 90 seconds, with at most 15 seconds for construction. Insufficient or timed-out preferred spaces leave the existing fallbacks available. PreferredPoleSpace and PreferredPoleFit retain the attempt outcome. CompleteHighEnergy preserves the recorded preference. BoseSymmetryGroups -> Automatic and FermionSymmetryGroups -> Automatic identify identical external states using the supplied model's twice-spin, masses, species and helicity. Even twice-spin uses symmetric permutations; odd twice-spin uses their parity signs. Electron and positron groups remain separate. ExternalParticles -> Automatic inherits ordered names retained in preparation reports. Pass ExternalParticles -> particles to PrepareAmplitudes or completion when compact pairs have lost the process names. Without names, only unambiguous model-and-spinor-state matches are projected; equal masses alone never identify a species. Opposite helicities, different fixed spin states, and color-stripped colored states are not merged automatically. Explicit disjoint groups remain supported and must be correct for the process. Each empty group option disables only that particle statistic; set both to {} to disable all exchange projection. The seed and correction directions are projected over the combined group, preserving every original residue target and the existing diagram and sewing signs. Automatic uses a bounded exact subgroup when the full combined group exceeds order 120; ExchangeSymmetry details expose detected and used groups, requested and used orders, FullGroupUsed, source and diagnostics. BoseSymmetry and FermionSymmetry give separate summaries. Completion combines available compact, literal and certified selected-cut-prepared channel terms before projection. Exact formal linear dependencies may be removed by sparse reduction within a 60-second budget; unfinished pruning retains the full space. MaxCorrectionTerms applies after projection and pruning. CorrectionSpaceCandidates records the available space sizes. Symmetry-union CorrectionSpace names begin with Bose for bosons only, Fermion for fermions only, and Exchange for both; SelectedChannelSpace records its selected-cut checks. Each intermediate source-space construction may grow with group order, capped at 4096 directions unless a larger MaxCorrectionTerms was requested. High-energy completion inherits the used exchange constraints from a detailed factorization report, including for newly generated correction directions. No successful reconstruction is claimed until every original target and the full fitted family pass independent validation. ShiftedChannelContinuations -> Automatic also tries up to four source-derived two-null-leg continuation proposals after cheap input/remainder routes, before wide correction spaces. Automatic requires at least three null and at most two massive external legs, matching the current compound-pole checker, and prefers opposite nonzero spin weights or identified null scalars. False or None disables this route; True permits a generic attempt beyond Automatic's support preference, with all original and final checks still required. Each direction is verified on its own original cut, then exact compact signed exchange averages are fitted against every original residue simultaneously. No shifted-sum formula or vanishing large-parameter boundary is assumed. Existing regular input pieces stay fixed; InputReweighting -> Automatic may fit the pole-bearing input core alongside the channel directions. Details retain ShiftedChannelContinuations, source checks, eligibility reasons, ShiftedChannelAttempts and ShiftedChannelFit. Unsupported, over-budget or nonclosing proposals fall back to the established routes."}

Genuine undetermined contact freedom remains UNDERDETERMINED, and sampled validation is not a generic uniqueness proof. Detailed preparation/factorization inputs preserve discarded diagram and channel shell remainders as bounded source-derived correction proposals. Their channel contour factors and sewing signs follow the residue checker. Automatic alternate parameter assignments vary independent model inputs, recompute dependent definitions and preserve explicit overrides; the fit uses the same correction coefficients across those assignments. No independent contact interaction is inferred from an unfinished or inconsistent fit."}

ConstructiveDiagrams`ConstructAmplitude.Messages: {HoldPattern[ConstructAmplitude::args] :> "Expected a process with at least four model particle names, a diagram model, a constructive factorization model, and valid construction options.", HoldPattern[ConstructAmplitude::usage] :> "ConstructAmplitude[process, diagramModel, factorizationModel] generates and prepares diagrams and factorization channels, completes factorization and high-energy behavior, prepares each completed expression with external identities only, then checks the final amplitude. The ordinary result is the bare expression only when every required final check passes. Output -> Amplitude returns {externalMassRules, expression}; Details retains stage results, timings and diagnostics. ProgressReporting -> True displays the current stage, its elapsed time and total elapsed time. At the end PrintReport -> True prints total time, the final SpinorExpressionComplexity score and the test table before returning the expression. FeynmanModel -> None optionally supplies an independent model whose diagrams are prepared and compared too. PreparationOptions, ChannelPreparationOptions, FinalPreparationOptions, FactorizationOptions, HighEnergyOptions, CheckOptions and FeynmanPreparationOptions pass options to individual stages. TimeConstraint -> Automatic selects a finite overall budget from the process and workload; individual stages resolve their own automatic limits. Explicit values override those choices. PolePreference -> AllPhysical is the default; AllSpurious prefers massless-reference forms and uses eligible physical replacements when needed. Mixed admits both. Final expressions resolve auxiliary Xi unless Xi, IndependentXi or None is requested. These choices leave validation intact. ParameterRules, HighEnergyBound, Samples, ValidationSamples, RandomSeed, Parallelization and MaxKernels provide common settings. The original channels remain the residue targets, discarded preparation terms and affine completion freedom are retained, and final preparation never applies internal-shell identities. Failed, opposite-sign and unresolved checks never produce a validated amplitude. With AllSpurious and a FeynmanModel, supported massive fermion lines with one opposite-helicity massless vector can first try a compact common-reference current derived from the diagram vertices. The current must pass the same amplitude checks before it is selected. For mixed helicities on a supported cubic vector line, a bounded off-shell construction uses the model vertices and shared massless references and returns the first validated form. For supported diagrams with two massive fermion lines and two external massless vectors, AllSpurious can group the photon attachments and contract the currents before expanding their spinor products. The constructor verifies the original cuts and exchange signs and accepts the result after independent validation. For supported six-fermion trees with no external vector legs, AllSpurious can combine the ordered fermion exchanges over their common physical vector propagators. The candidate is returned only after the original channel checks and independent Feynman comparison pass. A supported line with four external vectors of the same helicity can combine adjacent emission orders in pairs before validation. For larger AllPhysical processes with a supplied FeynmanModel, a certified minimal massive fermion line with same-helicity colorless vectors can combine photon subsets through ordinary off-shell Dirac identities. Every original residue and independent Feynman comparison must pass before this candidate is returned. For larger AllSpurious results with a FeynmanModel, a bounded compound-pole exchange reduction can propose a shorter form for independent validation. When FeynmanModel is supplied, a fixed factorization or high-energy candidate can be selected after every mandatory check and independent Feynman comparison passes; its unclassified affine family remains in Details and no uniqueness is claimed. Without that independent benchmark, unresolved completion freedom remains a failure. RandomSeed -> Automatic chooses one time-based run seed. The stages derive their seeds from that value, with explicit stage overrides honored. Details records RandomSeed and PrintReport prints it with the final timing; an explicit integer reproduces the sample choices. For larger AllSpurious lines with equal-helicity colorless vectors and a supplied FeynmanModel, a bounded terminal-pair and subset current uses the certified cubic vertices, external Dirac identities and momentum conservation. It keeps every internal propagator off shell and resolves all auxiliary references. Every original residue, apparent spurious pole, high-energy condition and independent Feynman comparison must pass before the candidate is returned. If an automatic high-energy timeout retains a fully solved point with every affine coordinate classified, a separate Validating retained HE candidate stage may use the remaining overall budget. It rechecks every original parameter assignment with the normal independent seeds and sample counts, and leaves the original child UNRESOLVED in Details. Explicit high-energy limits, unfinished classifications and known failed held-out checks cannot use this recovery. Final preparation and final checking remain required. With an independent FeynmanModel, supported five-leg color-singlet massive Dirac/scalar processes can first propose covariant currents matched exactly to every used elementary vertex and ordered diagram. A supported existing metric quartic is calibrated only from the complete known lower amplitude. Internal lines stay off shell, masses and couplings remain symbolic, and no benchmark or sampled coefficient fit constructs the proposal. It is accepted only after the original channels and all independent checks pass at every requested validation assignment. Default distinct-fermion inputs also receive an equal-independent-mass probe; explicit parameter and validation choices remain authoritative. Rejected or unsupported proposals retain the ordinary completion path."}

ConstructiveDiagrams`PhysicalPoleResidue.Messages: {HoldPattern[PhysicalPoleResidue::args] :> "Expected channel associations with Cut, Complement, Mass and ExternalLegs, and valid diagnostic options.", HoldPattern[PhysicalPoleResidue::usage] :> "PhysicalPoleResidue[expression, channel] extracts a pole coefficient. A list of channels extracts a compatible multiple-pole coefficient. Without a coherent KinematicMap the result is only FORMAL. A map f[expression, channels, poleVariables] must evaluate all spinors, momenta and propagators consistently near the selected cuts. KinematicKind distinguishes Sample from Symbolic charts. StructuralCoefficient -> True also computes the formal opaque-propagator coefficient by default; False skips that optional symbolic calculation and returns Missing[NotRequested] in its field without changing the mapped physical residue or kinematic validation. No internal on-shell condition is inferred from diagram mass rules."}

ConstructiveDiagrams`PrepareAmplitudes.Messages: {HoldPattern[PrepareAmplitudes::args] :> "Expected diagram {massRules, expression} pairs or compact factorization-channel rows, a model, and valid preparation options. All elements must declare consistent external masses.", HoldPattern[PrepareAmplitudes::usage] :> "PrepareAmplitudes[items, model] prepares diagram amplitude pairs or compact factorization-channel rows, preserving their input formats. Each element is prepared independently by ReduceSpinContractions, PolePreference replacement and ReduceSpinorProducts with physical propagators protected. AllSpurious compares eligible other-massless-particle references and uses a physical reference for any leg without one. AllPhysical compares momentum-insertion references giving physical poles outside that element's own cuts, and Mixed compares both types per external leg. Automatic compares admissible physical and spurious references and keeps the best completed trial. Cyclic and ReverseCyclic retain fixed reproducible spurious choices; Xi uses one common Xi0, IndependentXi one generic reference per external particle, and None retains input references. The best completed trial is ranked after ordinary spinor reduction and diagram-local numerator-shell reductions. MaxReferenceChoices -> Automatic resolves to a bounded 64-trial allowance; ReferenceTimeConstraint -> Automatic uses at most five seconds and one third of the remaining per-element TimeConstraint, shared with subsequent preparation. This is a bounded finite-reference search, not a global-minimum claim. ReturnDetails -> False is the default; True exposes inputs, assignments, tested alternatives, search limits, reductions and diagnostics. InternalOnShell -> True reduces known numerator scalar products using only that element's mass rules, including two-leg complements when MomentumConservation is True, before and after spinor reduction even at MaxSteps -> 0. False disables these internal-shell reductions and edits. Unknown invariants and denominators are not put on shell. A bounded improving identity search follows. Output -> \"Expression\" returns the prepared sum; \"Amplitudes\" preserves input formats; \"Details\" and ReturnDetails -> True request diagnostics. ReturnDetails takes precedence. Unavailable reference choices or an overall timeout remain PARTIAL. ProgressReporting, ProgressFunction, MaxSteps, MaxCandidates and MomentumConservation control preparation. No model vertices or factorization corrections are added. Ordinary ReduceSpinorProducts acts on the whole expression, including auxiliary denominators, with PropDen protected. Only external mass replacements act globally; internal replacements remain numerator-only. With MomentumConservation -> True, the bounded identity search also tries consistent whole-numerator external momentum eliminations and composite complements. Each trial is reduced before a strictly improving whole-expression rank is required. These trials use only declared external mass labels, share MaxSteps, MaxCandidates and the per-element time limit, and protect inverse factors from conservation and internal-shell substitutions. MomentumConservation -> False disables them. Enabled internal numerator cuts also supply simultaneous linear scalar-product relations, including differences of adjacent cuts. External momentum-conservation equations enter only when enabled. Inconsistent exact constraints remain PARTIAL. Reference trials checkpoint completed factored reductions before optional whole-product exploration; an interrupted exploration is not marked exhaustive. Bounded reciprocal massless-reference choices are tried after the original first tuple without increasing the time or choice limits. Input elements are detected individually: diagram {massRules, expression} pairs or compact factorization rows {m1, ..., mn, Multiparticle[cut], exchangedMass, expression}. The default output preserves each input element's format and metadata. Factorization rows supply only external shells and their selected cut; other propagators do not introduce shell assumptions. Channel 1/z factors and sewing signs are unchanged. Cut-only reductions preserve the selected residue, not an off-cut identity. Details add InputType, ElementTypes, ItemReports and ChannelReports. An unavailable reference choice returns Failure for ordinary output, for diagrams and channels alike; detailed output retains PARTIAL expressions and diagnostics. With a single external photon, AllSpurious uses the same eligible physical references as AllPhysical. With a FeynmanModel, only diagram pairs are accepted. Raw Feynman tensors are converted to spinor products before reference replacement and reduction; FermionHelicities supplies the helicities of massless Dirac external fields. Feynman preparation defaults to ordinary reduction with effective MaxSteps -> 0 unless MaxSteps is supplied explicitly; eager identity-route generation for large chains is opt-in. Feynman preparation always keeps every internal numerator and denominator off shell, regardless of InternalOnShell, and returns external-only mass rules. Existing propagators supply a separate reference-choice inventory, never shell assumptions. All Feynman diagrams use the same reference assignment per external leg: Automatic uses a fixed massless-particle cycle, or independent generic Xi references when fewer than two massless particles are available. AllSpurious and cyclic choices are deterministic rather than optimized separately per diagram. AllSpurious falls back to a shared physical reference for each leg without a spurious choice. AllPhysical uses deterministic momentum-insertion references from the shared process pole inventory, preferring massive external targets; its reference poles may coincide with a diagram's existing propagators. Xi, IndependentXi and None retain their meanings. Shared Mixed Feynman choices remain unimplemented and PARTIAL. Failed or timed-out conversion, or an unavailable requested reference choice, remains PARTIAL in details and returns Failure for ordinary output. Detailed output also retains RemainderData for every item. It separates the fixed-reference reduction difference from reference-continuation choices and retains each completed reduction and identity-step remainder without expanding it. ShellRemainder is the exact algebraic difference between the selected fixed-reference expression and the returned prepared expression, not a claim of off-cut equality. ReferenceContinuations retain common-Xi and, when unambiguous, shared per-external-leg Xi source expressions before internal-shell reductions. These are proposed continuations requiring full-amplitude validation. Partial preparation and missing or ambiguous reference information remain explicit. Ordinary amplitude-pair and channel-row outputs stay unchanged; pass detailed preparation reports to completion to use the retained data. A single {massRules, expression} pair is also accepted directly and returns a single pair by default. A completed amplitude carries external mass rules only: preparation applies ordinary reductions and reference choices without any internal-shell condition. Its existing propagators provide a separate reference-choice inventory, never numerator shell assumptions. Output -> Expression still returns the bare expression; details retain one-item OriginalAmplitudes and PreparedAmplitudes lists for reuse by completion. ExternalParticles -> Automatic leaves unspecified particle identities uninferred. An ordered list of model particle or antiparticle names can be supplied to retain process information in detailed output for later completion. Its length and exact external masses must agree with every item. Ordinary amplitude pairs and channel rows are unchanged; no process cache or global model assignment is created. Completed external-only amplitudes also try bounded sparse physical-denominator grouping, spinor-coefficient collection, exact off-shell propagator definitions and single-insertion conservation followed by null-momentum splitting. These add no internal-shell conditions and remain enabled at MaxSteps -> 0. The best completed checkpoint is retained; representation size and weighted expanded complexity are compared separately. Ranking reuse is bounded and local to this call. Completed external amplitudes also compare bounded shared-momentum determinant identities and ordinary six-spinor cofactors within their existing denominator groups. Exact scalar collection and accepted identity witnesses remain in details; only a strictly simpler complete checkpoint is returned. All kinematic inverse factors remain fixed, and no internal shell is added. Parallelization -> Automatic prepares independent items on available local kernels; MaxKernels -> Automatic uses the available processor and license limit. Set Parallelization -> False or MaxKernels -> 1 for serial execution. Feynman references are fixed once for the complete input before dispatch. Results retain input order, progress callbacks run only on the main kernel, and detailed output includes execution and fallback diagnostics."}

ConstructiveDiagrams`ValidateMadGraph.Messages: {HoldPattern[ValidateMadGraph::args] :> "Expected a generated SPINAS project directory, or incoming particle names -> outgoing particle names, helicity amplitude entries and a model, with valid validation options.", HoldPattern[ValidateMadGraph::usage] :> "ValidateMadGraph[directory] independently checks an exported SPINAS process against MadGraph at shared random physical momenta, with a separate result for every exported massless-helicity combination. ValidateMadGraph[particles, amplitude, model] checks one fixed-helicity all-ingoing expression. ValidateMadGraph[incoming -> outgoing, amplitudeEntries, model] first exports and builds a private SPINAS project. Massive spins are summed, not compared in potentially different spin bases. MadGraphPoints defaults to 1000 per helicity and MadGraphSeed -> Automatic chooses and reports a fresh replayable seed. Output -> Table returns a readable per-helicity table; Summary gives result counts and Details retains the complete numerical report and failed momenta. Specify MadGraphDirectory and MadGraphModel explicitly. Validation builds its comparison executable independently of optional MadEvent event-generation targets. MadGraphAllowedParticles -> All retains the selected theory; a list of positive absolute PDG codes, such as {11,22}, restricts intermediate particle types and includes their antiparticles. No theory or particle restriction is inferred from the HEPCAT model. MadGraphParameterMap and MadGraphParameterRules handle different parameter names or reference inputs. Squared amplitudes are compared, so overall phases do not affect the result. Colorless tree processes and certified coherent SU(3) color sums are supported; unsupported or unavailable comparisons are never reported as passing. This is numerical validation, not an analytic proof. Derived scalar couplings follow the supplied model definitions. For an explicitly selected sm or sm-full reference, verified tree-level model relations translate e, MW and sin(theta_W) into inverse alpha, Gf and MZ; explicit MadGraphParameterRules override these values. The reference must still supply compatible particle masses, Yukawa interactions and flavor mixing. Reports retain native SPINAS helicity labels. Outgoing massless-vector wavefunctions are mapped to HELAS's opposite label, while incoming vectors retain their label. The MadEvent callback applies the inverse conversion. The supplied amplitude and its normalization are unchanged."}

ConstructiveDiagrams`WriteSPINASProcess.Messages: {HoldPattern[WriteSPINASProcess::args] :> "Expected an output directory, all-ingoing amplitude entries, a model and valid export options, optionally preceded by incoming particle names -> outgoing particle names. The fixed-helicity form takes an ordered all-ingoing particle list and amplitude instead of entries.", HoldPattern[WriteSPINASProcess::usage] :> "WriteSPINASProcess[directory, particles, amplitude, model] writes a complete C++11 SPINAS process project for two incoming and at least two outgoing particles. The amplitude uses HEPCAT's all-ingoing convention; IncomingLegs -> {1,2} selects physical incoming legs and outgoing legs are crossed automatically, including angle-spinor signs. The project contains process.hpp, process.cpp, main.cpp, a deterministic physical phase-space example generator, CMakeLists.txt, README.md and manifest.json. SPINASDirectory -> Automatic looks for SPINAS_ROOT or the sibling spinas checkout; an explicit path overrides it. Model parameter defaults come from ModelParameterRules; ParameterRules overrides them locally. ProcessName sets a C++ class/executable name. Build -> True configures and links the project against the existing SPINAS library; RunExamples -> True also builds and runs three sample points. Precision -> Automatic reads the local SPINAS build configuration; LongDouble and Double are explicit choices. Overwrite -> False protects existing project files. ReturnDetails -> False normally returns the output directory; True adds file paths and build/run results. Fixed massless helicities are retained. amp2 averages incoming massive spins and sums outgoing massive spins at those fixed helicities, without an identical-particle phase-space factor or color sums/averages. Unsupported expressions return Failure before files are written; this function does not complete or validate the physical amplitude. The family overload WriteSPINASProcess[directory, {{particles1, amplitude1}, ...}, model] combines helicity-related amplitudes into one class. It fills identical-species, same-role massless leg permutations with their proper statistics sign. Missing identical-massless-boson permutations across physical roles are generated analytically before crossing, without inferring parity or missing zero amplitudes. Incomplete coverage is rejected before writing files. amp(ds1,...,dsn) and amp(Spins) select doubled spins and helicities; spin_sum sums all external spin/helicity states; amp2 also averages incoming states and includes the outgoing identical-species factorial factor, including identical fermions. Ordinary projects use persistent native SPINAS products and direct helicity branches; very large families retain canonical dispatch to bound source size. Color-stripped colored families are refused; full color families must retain their explicit color tensors. The original four-argument fixed-helicity overload retains its existing spin-sum and symmetry-factor conventions. Massless fermions marked L or R in the model contain only their physical chirality: particle and antiparticle helicities are opposite. Outgoing massless fermion helicities are crossed from the all-ingoing amplitude to the physical outgoing antiparticle. This leaves the established photon-helicity convention unchanged. A one-state chiral species is complete without a FixedHelicities selection and is not averaged over a nonexistent second state. CalcHEP can compare such complete chiral processes; a genuine restriction of a two-state species remains polarized and is unavailable to its unpolarized comparison. Full color amplitudes may contain ColorDelta, ColorGenerator, ColorStructure and ColorTrace with ColorIndex[leg]. A joint exact SU(3) basis preserves color interference and transforms its tensors with identical-particle helicity permutations. The generated class exposes color_amplitudes(spins), amp(spins,colors) and color_spin_sum(spins); spin_sum sums the coherent color square over spins and helicities, while amp2 additionally applies the incoming color average exactly once. A colored amp(spins) without explicit colors is ambiguous and is rejected. Independent CalcHEP and MadGraph comparisons support these certified full color sums. A bare stripped colored expression remains unsupported for family validation. Colored MadEvent and CalcHEP numerical integration are reported unavailable until their event adapters support the complete color representation. CMakeExecutable -> Automatic searches PATH and standard installation locations, including the macOS CMake application and Homebrew, so desktop Mathematica need not inherit the shell's PATH. An explicit full path selects another CMake installation. A missing build tool is reported before generating files; source-only export does not require CMake. WriteSPINASProcess[directory, incomingNames -> outgoingNames, amplitudeEntries, model] explicitly describes the physical process. The entries still contain all-ingoing particle lists and un-crossed formulas in that same leg order, with incoming legs first. Outgoing charged particle names are checked against the conjugate all-ingoing species. Generic massless names such as A sum their helicities; A.+ or A.- selects one. The established HEPCAT/SPINAS helicity sign convention is retained, and ReverseMomentum crosses outgoing momenta and angle spinors exactly once. FixedHelicities -> {leg -> doubledHelicity, ...} selects massless legs in either grouped overload. Only unfixed incoming helicities are averaged. A selected outgoing helicity gives a labeled contribution with the same identical-species phase-space factor. Complex amp calls preserve phases and include no spin sums, incoming averages or phase-space factors; coherent production-decay sewing is not performed by this exporter. Runnable projects currently require two incoming particles. Generated projects also contain validate_calchep(options) and a process_validate_calchep executable for an independent, seeded 1000-point comparison with an on-the-fly CalcHEP process. CalcHEPDirectory -> None and CalcHEPModel -> None leave reference validation unconfigured. Select the installation directory and CalcHEPModel -> {directory, number} explicitly. CalcHEPDirectory -> Automatic consults CALCHEP_ROOT or CALCHEP only. CalcHEPAllowedParticles -> All keeps the selected reference theory intact; an explicit list of positive absolute PDG codes, such as {11,22}, restricts internal particle types and includes their antiparticles. RunCalcHEPValidation -> True builds and runs this check, using CalcHEPPoints -> 1000 and CalcHEPSeed -> Automatic by default. Automatic chooses a seed from the time when validation runs and reports the concrete seed for replay; an explicit unsigned 64-bit integer fixes it. Complete unpolarized colorless processes and certified coherent SU(3) color sums are supported; genuinely polarized restrictions and stripped colored expressions report unavailable. Ordinary SPINAS execution does not require CalcHEP. If the CalcHEP numerical libraries are available, Build -> True links the runnable executable directly at build/results/n_calchep; there is no duplicate launcher in the build root. From build, enter results and run ./n_calchep. This uses CalcHEP's numerical menus, VEGAS, cuts and histograms with the exported SPINAS matrix element, without CalcHEP symbolic generation or a CalcHEPModel counterpart. Independent model parameters remain adjustable, dependent functions are recomputed, and mass/width changes are propagated. Fixed helicities remain labeled contributions. The ordinary SPINAS project remains usable without CalcHEP. CodeStyle -> Optimized is the default numerical backend: it analyzes expression dependencies to share per-point and per-spin calculations. CodeStyle -> Readable preserves the direct formula layout. Both retain identical complex-amplitude and spin-sum conventions. The manifest separates CodeStyle from CodeLayout and records optimization diagnostics. HelicitySymmetry -> Automatic reuses conjugate helicity contributions only when a bounded exact algebraic certificate succeeds. None keeps exhaustive sums. Conjugation explicitly declares the simultaneous helicity-reversal symmetry of the supplied family, as for tree-level vectorlike QED with real parameters and complete massive-spin sums. This declaration is a theory assumption, not an inference from numerical samples. Every individual complex amp and every helicity branch remains available. Selected helicity sets must contain both members of each pair; unsupported selections and nonzero-width expressions retain exhaustive sums. Any nonreal runtime parameter disables reuse. The manifest records the summation plan and its assumptions. Generated projects also expose validate_madgraph(options) and a process_validate_madgraph executable for independent fixed-massless-helicity validation. Specify MadGraphDirectory and MadGraphModel to select the independent installation and UFO theory. MadGraphAllowedParticles -> All retains all model particles; {11,22}, for example, restricts to electrons, positrons and photons using absolute PDG codes. MadGraphParameterMap relates differently named HEPCAT and UFO parameters; MadGraphParameterRules supplies explicit UFO external input values. RunMadGraphValidation -> True builds and runs MadGraphPoints -> 1000 shared points per helicity with MadGraphSeed -> Automatic. Fixed incoming or outgoing helicities are supported, and massive external spins are summed. The MadGraph validator allows a small absolute residual for exported exact-zero helicity sectors and records the residual and bound. When both reference checks are requested, both run independently even if the first fails. A failed requested check returns Failure with ExportResult retaining both reports and the generated files. Ordinary SPINAS execution does not require MadGraph. The same explicit MadGraph configuration also configures a PROC_<ProcessName> numerical process. An ordinary build creates that directory in the compiled export's build directory by default and supplies the exported HEPCAT/SPINAS matrix element to MadEvent integration, unweighting and event output. Build -> True prepares build/PROC_<ProcessName> without generating events. Run its bin/madevent native launcher; no process_madevent executable is created in the build root. The build prints the full HTML and event-output locations. Run and parameter cards adjust cuts, beams, masses and couplings. Fixed massless helicities and summed massive spins retain their specified averaging and symmetry factors. Current numerical coverage is colorless leading-order tree amplitudes; coherent decay sewing, NLO matching and a MadGraph massive-spin basis are not provided. The independent MadGraph validator continues to use MadGraph's own amplitude. After preparation, move or copy the complete PROC_<ProcessName> directory, for example PROC_eeAA, and start its bin/madevent program. The prepared directory contains the required HEPCAT/SPINAS amplitude files and libraries and no longer depends on the original exported project or build directory. MadGraph, Python, the Fortran toolchain and system libraries remain external prerequisites. Overwrite -> True lets the build regenerate an incompatible MadEvent session owned by the same export.
